newsitem.title: BELGIUM: China's Lu assures Europe over Hong Kong.
newsitem.headline: China's Lu assures Europe over Hong Kong.

text.p: China's man responsible for Hong Kong affairs, Lu Ping, sought to assure European politicians on Wednesday that the British colony's return to Chinese sovereignty on July 1 would not damage its economic well-being.
"July 1 is the day following June 30 and preceding July 2, that is all," he told a meeting of the European Parliament's foreign affairs committee.
Lu stressed Beijing would honour the spirit and letter of a deal giving Hong Kong special autonomous status as a Special Adminstrative Region (SAR) of China.
He said business confidence in the colony was high and property prices were booming in clear signals the business community did not fear China's intentions.

"I can assure you there will be complete freedom of religion in Hong Kong, that is for sure," he said, adding a little later: "We are not going to exclude any political parties from taking part in elections".
The European Commission also unveiled its new strategy for dealing with Hong Kong, saying that far from downgrading ties "1997 must mark another step forward in the relationship."

Sir Leon Brittan, the commissioner responsible for relations with China and Hong Kong, said the best way to support the "one country, two systems" concept on which a successful handover is based is for the EU to deal directly with the SAR where possible.

"The best way to make a reality of the high degree of autonomy promised for Hong Kong is for us all to deal directly with Hong Kong in the wide variety of policy areas for which it has been given responsibility," he wrote.

Sketching out the new EU policy towards Hong Kong, Brittan added that the human rights situation would be closely monitored, visa requests dealt with on their own merits, and direct economic ties put on a permanent footing.
